what_it_does: Multiplying large sets of numbers together is at the heart of running neural networks, and that multiplication is expensive in terms of chip area and power. One way to cut costs is to approximate multiplication using simpler integer addition via a mathematical trick called Mitchell's logarithm approximation. The problem is that this approximation introduces noticeable errors that can degrade model accuracy. This paper presents a framework called April that tackles both sides of that tradeoff: it adds a hardware-efficient correction step (based on down-sampling) to recover lost precision, and a flexible bias-adjustment mechanism to handle the wide variety of number distributions found across different neural network layers. The authors also create configurable hardware templates — pre-designed grid arrays of tiny multiplier units called systolic arrays — that can be automatically tuned to balance accuracy against chip resources, and a co-design tool that generates ready-to-manufacture chip blueprints.
